Run a read-only Claude Code agent and get structured output back

Source: R/agent_run.R
agent_run.Rd

Runs the Claude Code CLI (claude -p) once in workdir and returns its answer as an R object that matches a JSON Schema. The agent can read the files under workdir but cannot change them, run commands or reach the web.

Usage

agent_run(prompt, schema, workdir = ".", timeout = 600)

Arguments

prompt

The task, as a single string.

schema

A JSON Schema, as a single JSON string, that the answer must match. Write it as JSON text, not as an R list: converting a list with jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE) turns one-element arrays such as required into scalars and silently breaks the schema.

workdir

Path of an existing directory the agent works in. Its files are read in place, not copied.

timeout

Wall-clock limit for the whole run, in seconds. When it runs out, the CLI and all its child processes are killed.

Value

An object of class fmisc_agent_result, a list with:

value

The structured output, parsed by jsonlite::fromJSON() with default simplification (arrays of objects become data frames).

cost_usd

The CLI's estimated cost. Under a subscription this is not what you pay.

num_turns

Number of agent turns.

model

The model(s) the CLI actually used.

session_id

For correlation only; the session cannot be resumed.

permission_denials

Tool calls the CLI refused, which show when the agent tried to step outside read-only mode.

raw

The full parsed CLI result, for debugging. Not part of the stable contract.

Authentication and billing

agent_run() uses whatever login the claude CLI already has, meant to be the owner's Claude subscription (OAuth). It never reads, stores or passes tokens. These variables are removed from the child process's environment, so nothing set in the R session can switch the run to API billing, a gateway or a cloud provider: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (a subscription token from claude setup-token) passes through. cost_usd is the CLI's client-side estimate, not a bill. Use it for occasional, attended calls; it is not made for batch runs over many rows.

Isolation

The CLI runs with --safe-mode --restricted --strict-mcp-config, so CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers and settings files are not loaded. Only the Read, Glob and Grep tools are available, and any call that would need a permission prompt is denied (dontAsk, --permission-prompts none). The model (sonnet), the turn cap (20) and the budget cap (USD 1) are fixed. The prompt goes on stdin, never on the command line, and no session transcript is kept.

A fixed list of Read deny rules blocks common secret files at any depth: .env*, .Renviron*, .netrc, .git-credentials, *.pem, *.key, SSH keys (id_rsa*, id_dsa*, id_ecdsa*, id_ed25519*) and .ssh/. Claude Code applies these best-effort to Glob and Grep as well. This is defense in depth, not a sandbox: the agent can read every other file in workdir and send it to the model, including secrets under other names. Point workdir at a directory that holds only what the agent should see. Managed (policy) settings still apply.

Needs Claude Code CLI 2.1.259 or later on PATH. Not supported on Windows yet.

Errors

Every error inherits from fmisc_agent_error:

fmisc_agent_invalid_argument

A bad argument, including a schema that is not valid JSON. Raised before the CLI starts.

fmisc_agent_missing_package

processx or jsonlite is not installed.

fmisc_agent_cli_missing

claude is not on PATH.

fmisc_agent_timeout

The run hit timeout. Fields: timeout, stderr.

fmisc_agent_failed

The CLI exited non-zero, reported is_error, or printed output that is not JSON. Fields: exit_status, subtype (such as "error_max_turns"), stderr.

fmisc_agent_no_output

The run succeeded but returned no structured output, typically a refusal. Fields: subtype, permission_denials.

Messages never contain the prompt, the model's text or file contents.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
schema <- paste0(
  '{"type": "object", "required": ["functions"], "properties": ',
  '{"functions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}}'
)
res <- agent_run(
  "Which exported functions in this package have no examples?",
  schema = schema,
  workdir = "."
)
res$value$functions
res
} # }
